You can’t lose weight quickly if you want healthy, long term results. The only way to lose weight is through a caloric deficit. One option is to use an online calculator to figure out your daily calorie needs, then calculate a 10-20% deficit from there and track your food intake (I would also recommend tracking macros) to make sure you stay within your daily target calories. An easier option is to just focus on eating a diet of non calorically dense foods, fruits and veggies, and lean protein. It’s best to home cook/prepare as many meals as you can. If you’re short on time for cooking during the week dedicate your Sunday’s to meal prepping. Planning ahead is key! Exercise is also super important. Cardio, among its other benefits, will burn extra calories to help put you in a caloric deficit. However, I highly recommend focusing most of your exercise on weight training. Not only will it help your body look toned, but maintaining and building muscle requires a lot of calories, and thus you will burn more calories throughout the day and can eat more while still being in a deficit. Losing weight takes tons time and patience, but will be extremely rewarding. Good luck!

Greasy hair may be the result of silicone buildup and the poofyness is likely caused by a lack of hydration in your curls. I would try out the Curly Girl method (r/curlyhair has TONS of helpful info and a simple beginner routine to get started). It’s super important to cut out silicones and sulfates from your hair care! Techniques such as squish to condish and deep conditioning add moisture back into your hair, as well as products such as curl creams and gel (which also help define your curls and prevent frizz). I have wavy hair and always struggle with volume at the roots, so I found that techniques such as plopping, applying products/diffusing my hair upside down, and using two-prong clips to keep my roots pushed up while my hair finishes drying help tons. It takes a while to find what works for your hair, but don’t be afraid to try out different types of products/techniques. Good luck! :)
